title: Speculative Safety Honeypot: Toward Proactive Defense Against Multi-turn Agent Attacks
src: abstract-only: lacuna.tiptreesystems.com summary page (ICML 2026); arxiv.org abs/html/html-v1/pdf for 2609.39549 all returned HTTP 429

title: MaMa: A Game-Theoretic Approach for Designing Safe Agentic Systems
src: arxiv.org/html/2602.04431v2 (ICML 2026 camera-ready text); v1 date from paperswithcode.co (arXiv abs page showed no history)
evidence: Adversary 'can select and overwrite a subset of ε agents'. Meta-Agent (GPT-5.1) designs agents/topology/tools at design time; designed systems add reviewer/approver agents ('a third agent approves the action'). Meta-Adversary searches strongest attacks against each candidate system; 'Table 2 depicts the results with varying models for both the Meta-Adversary at deployment time, and the agents' models' -> search-based attack against final system. policy_src=LLM means design-time LLM-generated architecture. Main agent model Llama-3.3-70B plus varied models (count unclear). Design cost $72.15, 2-4 days per env.

title: Causal Detection of Multi-Step LLM Agent Attacks
src: abstract-only: icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/64714 + lacuna.tiptreesystems.com summary; no arXiv version found by search
evidence: CausalTrace builds structural causal models from agent trajectories and uses do-calculus to test 'whether the harmful outcome would have occurred if the injection had been blocked'; summary says 'optimized for post-hoc audits (analyzing logs after execution)' (detect-only). >99% F1 CausalBench, 92.6% F1 OOD; FP 0.011% on 27k benign trajectories; 0.15ms slice time. Summary lists 'structure-aware' adversaries mimicking benign causal topologies as limitation (suggests 0, not confirmed from full text).

title: SafeHarbor: Defining Precise Decision Boundaries via Hierarchical Memory-Augmented Guardrail for LLM Agent Safety
src: arxiv.org/html/2605.05704 (ICML 2026 camera-ready text; version not shown; abs/pdf unreadable via fetch)
evidence: Malicious users issue harmful instructions. Two-stage gate on the query: MLP projector S_harm + benign similarity; 'For queries falling into the ambiguous or risky zones ... we introduce an LLM Judgment mechanism' using retrieved hierarchical memory of LLM-generated prohibition rules/exemptions; refuse or execute. Enhanced attacks (Goal Decomposition, Privilege Escalation, Contextual Reframing) are generic augmentations, not optimized vs SafeHarbor -> 0. Models: GPT-4o, Mistral-8B, Qwen2.5-7B + GPT-5, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen3-32B. 306.67 ms avg latency; benign refusal 9.1% vs LlamaGuard 22.7%. v1 date not retrievable (ID implies May 2026).

title: Learning When to Act or Refuse: Guarding Agentic Reasoning Models for Safe Multi-Step Tool Use
evidence: MOSAIC post-trains agent (RL w/ pairwise LLM-judge rewards) into plan->safety_thoughts->act-or-refusal_tool loop before each tool call; evaluates direct and 'indirect injections introduced through adversarial tool responses'. No attack designed/optimized against MOSAIC -> 0. Models Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-4B-Thinking, Phi-4. Safety reasoning <20% of tokens; Phi-4 benign refusal 0.43->0.19.

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Corruptions via Node Contribution Backpropagation
evidence: Malicious agents inject misleading info. After the final decision, signed temporal DAG; LLM scores edges g_ij in {-1,0,1}; backward contribution propagation + threshold flags agents; 'removing all outgoing messages from agents in M' then re-run (post-hoc repair). Adaptive: §4.6 corrupted nodes 'deliberately alter the score'; §4.7 'System-Aware (SA) adaptive attack' given 'the global topology, the scoring mechanism, and current neighborhood scores' -- knowledge-based, no optimization loop -> 1. DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o. ~9-10.6% time overhead.

title: Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents
bench: own:data subject-sender-recipient privacy simulation (115 configs seeded from PrivacyLens)
evidence: Attacker = data recipient agent extracting private info. Proposed CDI: separate RL-trained instructor LLM reads context (incl. recipient messages, tool results) and injects step-specific privacy guidance before next action; also compares RL-trained guard (pre-execution ALLOW/BLOCK) and prompting. 'our attack algorithm was optimized on CDI with Qwen3-4B as the instructor model' (iterative search-based attack vs defended system) -> 2. Agent backbones gpt-4.1-mini + 3 others. Helpfulness score captures over-restriction. public_bench=N: own simulation, only seeds from PrivacyLens. No inference overhead numbers.

title: *MemPot*: Defend Against Memory Extraction Attack with Optimized Honeypots
evidence: Memory-extraction attacker with normal user privileges; optimized honeypot memories (contrastive embedding optimization + inversion) inserted into memory; SPRT over honeypot retrievals across rounds; block ('Unanswerable') when Λt ≥ log A. Threat model: attackers 'have no prior knowledge of the defense setting'; no adaptive eval -> 0. Backbone DeepSeek-v3.2. Zero online latency vs 0.03-0.4s baselines; TPR@1%FPR; WebShop SR 44.6->43.8.

title: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents
bench: own:MT-AgentRisk (multi-turn tasks derived from OpenAgentSafety, SafeArena, P2SQL, MCPMark)
evidence: Adversarial user distributes harmful intent across turns. ToolShield: LLM generates test cases from tool docs, runs them in sandbox, distills safety experiences offline, 'injected into the agent's context at deployment'; agent itself refuses. No attack aware of/optimized against ToolShield -> 0. Defended models: GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, Gemini-3-Flash, Seed-1.6, Qwen3-Coder, DeepSeek-v3.2. Experience generation cost $0.16-$1.06; benign success 95.3->94.1%, benign RR 0%. Only own benchmark used for ToolShield.

title: When Embedding-Based Defenses Fail: Rethinking Safety in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
bench: MMLU;GSM8K;BBH (own MAS attack settings incl. Slow Drift, Benign Wrapper, Chaos Seeding)
evidence: Compromised agents with adversarial system prompt. Proposed confidence-guided defense: token-entropy confidence threshold prunes low-confidence messages before delivery, or attaches confidence for receiving agent to down-weight. New near-benign attacks target prior embedding-based defenses (G-Safeguard, GUARDIAN), not designed against the proposed confidence defense -> 0. LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B, GPT-4o-mini. No overhead or benign-message FP numbers.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Protecting LLM Agents Against Tool Description Poisoning via Isolated Planning
evidence: Attacker poisons descriptions of non-sensitive tools. Tool-Guard partitions tools into Influenced/Others lists, plans under isolation, then LLM alignment + suspicion checks before execution (validator sees user query and prior validated observations, excludes poisoned descriptions); failure moves tool to Influenced list and replans. Adaptive: manual alignment-/suspicion-adaptive descriptions, and 'For optimization-based adaptive attacks, we evaluate our defense using PAIR ... and TAP' -> 2. Models: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-pro/flash, Claude-3.5-haiku, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo. ~1.4-1.45x tokens, ~3.7x runtime. Utility only, no FP rate.

title: PrivGate: Steering Contextual Integrity in LLMs via Latent Space Geometry
src: abstract-only: icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/61631 + papers.cool (OpenReview abstract); no arXiv version found by search
evidence: Contextual-integrity leakage (no attacker described in abstract). Latent Gating: training-free linear 'privacy manifold' signal in residual stream 'triggers explicit reasoning only when high latent risk is detected' (base LLM reasons itself). 62.6% relative leakage reduction with 15.9% token overhead. Enforcement point not stated in abstract.

title: MINIM: Privacy-Aware Minimal View for Agents via Trusted Local Sanitization
src: arxiv.org/html/2606.13949 (ICML 2026 camera-ready text; version not shown; abs page showed no history)
bench: own:WebArena-derived accessibility trees with synthetic sensitive content (5,403 variants)
evidence: Honest-but-curious remote agent server; prompt-injection adversaries out of scope. Trusted local GATv2 predicts sensitivity and task-conditioned necessity per UI node, fixed mapping to Remove/Abstract/Keep before transmission. No attack vs sanitizer -> 0. No end-to-end agent run (n_models=0); utility only as TCNP/TCNP-I node-preservation proxy (0.949/0.993), counted as over-removal measure for fpr. No latency numbers. v1 date not retrievable (ID implies Jun 2026).

title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework For LLM-Based Agent Memory
evidence: Poisoned memory via direct write or indirect query injection. For each retrieved memory, LLM builds reasoning paths, consensus divergence filters anomalous memories; failures distilled into 'lessons' consulted before actions to revise plan. Only stronger existing attacks ('black-box probing to optimize the trigger query') -- not designed vs A-MemGuard -> 0. GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3.1-8B. Appendix E token cost analysis (numbers not extracted). No FP rate.

title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
evidence: Attacker controls user prompts. Representation Rerouting (LoRA) makes the model itself interrupt harmful generations incl. harmful function calls. 'we also introduce three powerful attacks that leverage system-level and representation-space access' (prefilling, input-embedding, RepE attacks) plus GCG/PAIR/TAP run against the defended models -> 2. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v2, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B. WildChat refusal 2.0->3.4% / 2.2->6.2%. No inference overhead numbers (only '20 minutes' training).
